q.metric: Q = mean over the 8 builds of (scenarios passed / scenarios of runtime-ab-rep that the build was scored on); a build that did not start counts 0 and is reported apart; flakes are left out as in flakeRule
q.ceilingNote: ceiling = Q >= 95 (calibrate-80's ceilingPct). Basis: lap 13 (A alone, 495 words) 100.0 %; the calibration's opus minimum was 90.6 % over 12 requests of 694-901 words and 96.2 % at L2; B adds a fail-safe rule that the request states as a principle plus one sentence, not rule by rule. The prediction is one-sided on purpose: the owner asked for a request 'that may split', not for a request chosen to split, so the side follows the evidence, and the evidence says a Q below 90 % is the less likely side.
q.bandNote: pBelow90 = 0.25 is for the whole lap, including a 0.10 share for a lap-invalidating infrastructure fault that would show as Q near 0 (see dependency-resolution); builder-caused Q below 90 % is about 0.15-0.20

whereItFalls.note: Where the first failing scenario of a build is expected, as probabilities that at least one build (of 8) fails at least one scenario for that reason. They do not sum to 1. 'dependency' and 'base' are lap-invalidating (infrastructure, not a builder verdict); the rest are builder verdicts or expectation errors.

sites.how: B's fail-safe: after an invalid input (not JSON, a missing field) or an unwritable --state-dir, the earlier record of that target must be gone. A build removes the record only for wait/escalate and leaves it after invalid input or after a failed write; or it keeps the old record when the new write fails
sites.reading: the site the request states least rule by rule (a principle and one sentence); the most likely builder-caused failure

sites.how: a scenario compares `decide_argv` exactly (order, the value of --state-dir). The request fixes the order (after --deadline-ms: --target, --task-id, --state-dir) but not whether --state-dir is the string given or a normalised path (`./s` vs `s`, trailing slash); builds differ, and the scenario's expectation may follow one of them
sites.reading: if the scenario drafter assumed one reading and the request does not decide it, it is an expectation error (errors.json), not a builder failure

sites.how: a build accepts `.hidden`, `a/b`, `..` or an empty target, or rejects a legal one (`a.b-c_1`), or touches a file for an invalid target
sites.reading: builder verdict; the pattern is stated in words, so most builds should pass

sites.reading: lap 13 passed this site in 8 of 8 builds, so it is lower than in lap 13's registration (0.35)

sites.how: a scenario asserts a value of decided_at_ms (an absolute time or a window around now) that no build can meet reliably, or compares the records of two passes by time
sites.reading: expectation error: errors.json and out of Q (the request says only that expires_at_ms - decided_at_ms is 30000)

successLine.text: The lap 'held' (factory carried over to an existing Python repository at a size that may split) when all of: (1) Q >= 90 %; (2) at least 7 of the 8 builds started (builderOk); (3) no lap-invalidating fault (dependency-resolution or base-move) in any scored scenario; (4) the run shipped: runtime-ab-run ended with a fast-forward of the ship target whose new HEAD is the judged commit and which has 003efef as an ancestor. Otherwise 'did not hold', and the report names the site of the first failure by the whereItFalls list. A lap-invalidating fault is not a verdict on the builder: it is reported as invalid and the replicate is run again under a new change id after the fault is fixed. Conditions (2)-(4) are carried over from lap 13; the owner's line is (1).
successLine.linesNote: the 80 % line of lap 13 is not used. Q is read against 90 % and the result is also placed against lap 13 (100.0 % at 495 words) and calibrate-80 (opus: no Q below 90.6)

errorsRule: Errors rule (lap 8, restated): an expected value that contradicts the request, or a count or number that does not add up, is an expectation error; so is a run step whose expectation depends on a file or a template path the shown ranges do not give, and an expectation that depends on a reading the request leaves open (decide-argv-values: the form of --state-dir) or on the clock (clock-in-expectation). Each is listed in errors.json with a quote of the request; the whole scenario is left out of every build's pass fraction. Q is reported both raw and corrected; if they fall on different sides of 90 %, the verdict is 'undecided', not either.
flakeRule: Flake rule (lap 12, restated): each build is rescored twice after its first judgement (replicate --rescore twice, judgements = 3). A (scenario, build) whose pass/fail differs among the 3 is a flake and is left out of that build's pass fraction (numerator and denominator). More than 5 % of the cells being flakes gives no verdict.

comparability.summary: Q here uses the same formula as calibrate-80 and lap 13 (mean over builds of a build's pass fraction). It is read against the owner's 90 % line and placed beside lap 13 and the calibration; it is not a point on the calibration curve.
differences: a command-line program with `run` steps (exit code, stdout JSON, files), not an HTTP app, as in lap 13
an extension of an existing repository (152 tracked files); calibration builds started from an empty repository
K=8 builds of one spec, one scenario set (own only); calibration used 4 builds x 2 sets (own and cross) per request
the scenario count is not fixed in advance (calibration: 11-15; lap 13: 14; here an expected 26-34); each scenario is worth less of Q than in lap 13

request size is 1,082 words: above calibrate-80's L0 (694-901), below its L1 (1,614-1,798), 2.2 times lap 13. The calibration's finding that Q does not fall with size covered 694-3,594 words on greenfield apps
two changes in one request, joined at one output (decide_argv); calibration's combined requests joined 2-4 parts with 10-49 cross rules, and this one has 1 (Part 3)
the drafters and the classifier saw only the ranges, the builder the whole repository; calibration drafters saw the whole (empty or small) app
the builder is claude-opus-5-5, as in the calibration; no cross-family scenario drafter
dependencies are provided from a hash-pinned set outside the sandbox (lap 13's set, reused)
one-sided line: 90 % (calibrate-80 and lap 13 used 80 % for 'does not drop')

contamination.text: Both subjects are public in suisya-systems/claude-org-runtime: A is #242 / issue #240 (merged 2026-10-11), B is #245 / issue #244 (merged 2026-10-12); both released in v0.1.50. A model may have seen them, so Q can be an upper bound on what the builder derives from the request alone. Leak paths: (1) model training data, not testable here; (2) the builder's model session shares the host network (factory README), so a builder could read the published fix or `pip download` a released wheel of claude-org-runtime; the run contract tells it to install nothing and use no network, an instruction only; (3) the ship target holds no object after 003efef. B's section of docs/cli.md is not in the base (it was added by the change), so the base holds no written answer to B. The request states the rules of both changes in its own words, so the builder is not asked to rediscover them. No forward-looking subject is used in this lap (runtime #21, ntfy, needs a fake service the run step cannot reach, laps/lap-14/design.md).
contamination.check: after the replicate and the run, every builder transcript under $FACTORY_HOME/transcripts/<change>/ (factory prerequisite 1) is searched; the commands are in runbook step 9. Search terms: `github.com/suisya-systems/claude-org-runtime`, `raw.githubusercontent`, `pypi.org`, `pip download`, `pip install`, `git fetch`, `git log --all`, the commit ids b6ad40a / 263ff3f / 410fd8a / 176bcf1 / a021ebd / 719f865 / f79286f, the tags v0.1.50 / v0.1.51, the issue numbers #240 / #242 / #244 / #245, and the tool names WebFetch / WebSearch. Any hit lists the build apart and Q is given with and without it. A transcript that is missing for a build is itself reported (the check is then incomplete, not clean). The check is on the transcript, the output-side search over the build's diff (as in lap 13) is run too.
